A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical study. Their main text, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated bounds and proofs can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 presents analytical counterexamples, convergence bounds, and stability proofs. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: V2 remains a theoretical paper. Its expanded explanations and revised proofs do not introduce experiments, simulations, user studies, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: SA-ERM, SA-GD, and normalized-gradient SAM retain the same procedures in Equations 3–5. Expanded construction sketches and proof revisions do not change these algorithms.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or tasks experimentally. The constructed distributions are analytical counterexamples, not added training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparisons with GD and SGD remain theoretical and unchanged. Neither version introduces an evaluated experimental baseline.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, computational budgets, or testing procedures. Parameters appearing in the bounds specify theoretical conditions.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or case studies appear in either version. The expanded proof sketches explain existing analytical counterexamples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Probabilities in the theorems are analytical guarantees rather than uncertainty estimates from experiments.

E6.justification: Neither version contains measured outcomes or empirical result entries. The principal qualitative separations and asymptotic convergence and population-risk rates remain unchanged; revisions to theoretical constants are covered under T1.

T1.justification: V1 Lemma 4 becomes v2 Lemma 2 with bounded coordinates for z, an added 1/2 prefactor, and a revised projection-based smoothness argument. The SAM lower-bound construction changes from 7-Lipschitz in v1 Theorem 6 to 6-Lipschitz in v2 Theorem 7, with a revised supporting derivation. The main bounds and counterexample mechanisms are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal separation claims are unchanged. V2 Section 1.1 newly emphasizes that population-risk upper and lower bounds nearly match, adding an explicit tightness claim to the existing upper-bound contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 6 substantially expands applicability qualifications: the separation depends on worst-case losses, distributions, oracles, and hyperparameters; constructions require exponential dimension; and smaller perturbation-radius regimes remain unresolved. V2 also explicitly discusses remaining upper/lower-bound gaps. V1 contains only scattered, narrower caveats.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation, hardware, runtime, code-access, or dataset-access information. Expanded mathematical explanations do not disclose a new implementation or experimental configuration.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Author-year citation formatting and the updated title and publication information for Evron et al. replace matching references rather than add new research.

P1.justification: V2 replaces the consolidated results overview with separate SA-ERM, SA-GD, and SAM sections, integrates previously appended population-risk bounds, and reorganizes the appendices accordingly. Expanded proof sketches, a new discussion section, and conversion to author-year citations substantially revise the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Neither version contains figures or tables. V2 reformats Equations 3–4 into stacked displays and redisplays existing constructions within expanded main-text sketches. The overall single-column design is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the existing results easier to assess through clearer organization, fuller proof explanations, corrected lemma assumptions and scaling, and substantive worst-case limitations. These gains outweigh a localized new summary error: Section 1.1 states an O(eta^2 r^2 T) excess term, whereas the retained formal bound in Theorem 4 contains eta beta^2 r^2 T. The improvement is useful but limited.
